page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre with page number at top right. Three woodcut illustrations, each followed by its caption in full-width lines below it. No marginal notes. Reading order: running head and page number; first woodcut; its caption; second woodcut; its caption; third woodcut; its caption at the foot.

main_text.l: Nautæ in dorsa Cetorum, quæ insulas putant, ancoras figentes, sæpe periclitantur. Hos cetos Tralual sua lin­
Similis est & illorum icon apud eundem, capite, rostro, de-
ntibus, fistulis: quos montium instar grandes esse scri­
bit, & naues euertere, nisi sono tubarum aut missis in mare rotundis & uacuis uasis absterreantur. Idem in Balthi­co
ZIPHIVS (Ziphio simile, in libello Germanico) monstrum marinum horribile, Phocam ni­
gram deglutiens. Monstrum etiam aliud innominatum terribile Ziphio ad latus insidiatur,
ut Olai pictura repræsentat. Ziphij quidem nomen recentius est, non multò ante Alberti sæcu

page.notes: Three woodcuts: a whale-like sea monster with sailors on its back and a ship; a sea monster with spouting fountains beside a ship; a large horned sea monster attacking a smaller creature. The caption "Tralual" and "Teüfelwal" are printed in black letter. The first word of the third caption is a large woodcut initial Z, read as ZIPHIVS. The final line is cut off at the foot of the page.
